Extract the results of several NONMEM runs

Source: R/nm_extract_runs.R
nm_extract_runs.Rd

Extract the results of several NONMEM runs

Usage

nm_extract_runs(path, runs = NULL, verbose = TRUE)

Arguments

path

Analysis directory, or the directory of a single run.

runs

Optional names of the runs to keep.

verbose

Print progress.

Value

An object of class nm_runs with:

  • $runs: one row per run

  • $params: one row per parameter (same = TRUE for the OMEGA elements of an $OMEGA ... SAME record)

  • $mixture: for $MIX runs with a .phm file, one row per subject and subpopulation (PMIX, assigned = most probable subpopulation)

  • $path: the analysis directory

  • $created: time of extraction

Details

When the control stream of a run is found, parameters are named from the model code with nm_identify_parameters(): typical-value THETAs and ETAs after the PK parameter they act on (CL, V...), covariate-effect and residual-error THETAs after their $THETA comment label when it is a short name (CL_WT, PROP, ADD...). Other THETAs keep their NONMEM name (THETA6...).

Several estimation steps, several problems, failed runs

With several $EST records, the OFV, the minimisation status, the shrinkage and the covariance step are those of the last estimation step (est_methods lists the steps, e.g. "ITS > SAEM > IMP(eval) > FOCEI"). With several $PROB, the last problem that has an estimation is read (n_problems). The estimates are read in the .ext; when it is empty, has no final row, or reports an OFV different from the .lst (an .ext left by another run), they are read in the .lst (params_source) and a warning is given. run_state is "completed", "interrupted" (the output stops before the end of the last step), "terminated" (PROGRAM TERMINATED), "nmtran_error" or "simulation" (simulation-only run, $SIMULATION ONLYSIM, finished: no OFV, min_ok is NA; subproblems are not counted in n_problems). n_omega and n_sigma count the estimated elements only (not FIX, not SAME, not the zeros outside the blocks); n_eta_same counts the ETAs declared SAME (inter-occasion variability); ETAs fixed to 0 are left out of max_eta_shrink. For $MIX runs, n_subpop is the number of subpopulations, the mixing-proportion THETAs are named MIX_P when they have no other name, the shrinkage of an ETA is its smallest value over the subpopulations, and mix_assign counts the subjects assigned to each subpopulation.
